brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

finish.summary: I built a small 3-level hex shelf unit with 16 parts: 7 bases, 3 snaps, 4 joint bolts and 2 drawers. The drawers sit in two half bases on either side of the bottom of the centre column. Above them are full-base shelf cells: the column at (0,0) is 3 levels high and the one at (0,-1) is 2. All four joints between side-by-side bases have bolts. check_build shows no rule errors and meshClash "clear". It also lists 28 faces that could take caps; I left these open. Each cell is about 190 × 170 × 80 mm, so these are small cubbies and only small books will fit. The 50 kg rating is not verified: the tool checks fit, not strength.

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit (several levels of open storage)
requirements.evidence: Full bases piece:0,0,0 / 0,0,1 / 0,0,2 and piece:0,-1,0 / 0,-1,1 make 3 levels of shelf cells. They are joined by snaps and joint bolts (jointBolt:0#0,-1#5, 1#0,-1#5, 0#-1,0#1, 0#0,0#0). check_build: no errors, meshClash clear.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut sit on the cut faces of the half bases piece:-1,0,0;half-n and piece:1,0,0;half-n. Both open to the south.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only, not strength, so no load rating can be claimed or verified. The cells are about 190 × 170 × 80 mm, so books bigger than that won't fit. The load needs separate engineering and testing.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
